entries.name: alloc(
entries.notes: Allocate n bytes of memory, return address

entries.name: analog(
entries.notes: Read voltage level on pin n — returns a value from 0 to 4095

entries.name: asc(
entries.notes: Return ASCII value of first character or zero for empty string

entries.name: assert
entries.notes: Error generated if {expr} is zero, with optional message.

entries.name: atan(
entries.notes: Arctangent of n in degrees

entries.name: atan2(
entries.notes: Arctangent 2 calculation, dy / dx => angle

entries.name: by
entries.notes: Same as to but x and y are an offset from the current position

entries.name: call
entries.notes: Call named procedure with optional parameters.

entries.name: cat
entries.notes: Show contents of current directory, can take an optional string which only displays filenames containing those characters, so cat "ac" only displays files with the sequence ac in them.

entries.name: chr$(
entries.notes: Convert ASCII to string

entries.name: clear
entries.notes: Clear out stack, strings, reset all variables. If an address is provided then memory above that will not be touched by BASIC. Note because this resets the stack, it cannot be done in a loop, subroutine or procedure — they will be forgotten. Also clears the sprites and the sprite layer.

entries.name: close
entries.notes: Close a file by handle. If the handle is not provided, close all files.

entries.name: cls
entries.notes: Clear the graphics screen to current background colour. This does not clear sprites.

entries.name: cos(
entries.notes: Cosine of n, n Is in degrees.

entries.name: cursor
entries.notes: Set the text cursor position

entries.name: data
entries.notes: DATA statement. For syntactic consistency, strings must be enclosed in quote marks e.g. data

entries.name: deek(
entries.notes: Read word value at a

entries.name: defchr
entries.notes: Define UDG ch (192-255) as a 6x7 font — should be followed by 7 values from 0-63 representing the

entries.name: delete
entries.notes: Delete a line or range of lines

entries.name: dim
entries.notes: Dimension a one or two dimension string or number array, up to 255

entries.name: dim
entries.notes: Set the scaling to n (for TEXT, IMAGE, TILEMAP only), so text "Hello" dim 2 to 10,10 to 10,100 will draw it twice double size. Tiles can only be 1 or 2 (when 2, tiles are drawn double size giving a 32x32 tile map)

entries.name: do
entries.notes: General loop you can break out of at any point.

entries.name: doke
entries.notes: Write word to address

entries.name: edit
entries.notes: Basic Screen Editor

entries.name: ellipse
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws a circle or ellipse (solid = filled, frame = outline).

entries.name: end
entries.notes: End Program

entries.name: eof(
entries.notes: Returns non-zero value if at end of file f.

entries.name: erl
entries.notes: Current error line number

entries.name: err
entries.notes: Current error number

entries.name: event(
entries.notes: event takes an integer variable and a fire rate (r) in 1/100 s, and uses the integer variable to return -1 at that rate. If the value in 'v' is zero, it resets (if you pause say), if the value in v is -1 the timer will not fire — to unfreeze, set it to zero and it will resynchronise.

entries.name: exists(
entries.notes: Returns true (-1) if the file exists, false (0) otherwise

entries.name: exp(
entries.notes: e to the power n

entries.name: false
entries.notes: Return constant 0, improves boolean readability

entries.name: fkey
entries.notes: Lists the defined function keys

entries.name: fkey
entries.notes: Define the behaviour of F1..F10 — the characters in the string

entries.name: for
entries.notes: For loop. Note this is non standard,Limitations are : the index must be an integer. Step can only be 1 (to) or -1 (downto). Next does not specify an index and cannot be used to terminate loops using the 'wrong' index.

entries.name: forward
entries.notes: Move turtle forward n (pixel distance)

entries.name: frame
entries.notes: Just draw the outline of rectangles and ellipses

entries.name: from
entries.notes: Sets the origin position, can be repeated and optional.

entries.name: gload
entries.notes: Load filename into graphics memory.

entries.name: gosub
entries.notes: Call subroutine at line number. For porting only. See goto.

entries.name: goto
entries.notes: Transfer execution to line number. For porting only. Use in general coding is a capital offence. If I write RENUMBER it

entries.name: havemouse(
entries.notes: Return non zero if a mouse is connected.

entries.name: himem
entries.notes: First byte after end of memory — the stack is allocated below here, and string memory below that.

entries.name: hit(
entries.notes: The hit function is designed to do sprite collision. It returns true if the pixel distance between the centre of sprite 1 and the centre of sprite 2 is less than or equal to the distance.

entries.name: idevice(
entries.notes: Returns true if i2c device present.

entries.name: if
entries.notes: Standard BASIC if, executes command or line number. (IF .. GOTO doesn't work, use IF .. THEN nn)

entries.name: if
entries.notes: Extended multiline if, without THEN. The else clause is optional.

entries.name: image
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws a sprite or tile image n. dim sets the scaling ; solid forces black background.

entries.name: ink
entries.notes: Set the ink foreground and optionally background for the console.

entries.name: ink
entries.notes: Draw in solid colour c

entries.name: ink
entries.notes: Draw by anding the colour with a, and xoring it with x.

entries.name: inkey$(
entries.notes: Return the key stroke if one is in the keyboard buffer, otherwise returns a n empty string.

entries.name: input
entries.notes: Input has an identical syntax and behaviour to Print except that variables are entered via the keyboard rather than printed.

entries.name: input
entries.notes: Reads a sequence of variables from the open file.

entries.name: input
entries.notes: Reads text from an ASCII file. This is processed from the source, primarily due to Windows' usage of CR/LF. So this at current, by default, ignores all characters before space, except for LF (10) which marks the end of line, and TAB (9) which is converted into a space. All variables are strings

entries.name: instr(
entries.notes: Returns the first position of search$ in str$, indexed from 1. Returns zero if not found.

entries.name: int(
entries.notes: Whole part of the float value n. Integers are unchanged.

entries.name: iread(
entries.notes: Read byte from I2C Device Register

entries.name: ireceive
entries.notes: Send or receive bytes starting at a, count s to or from device d.

entries.name: isend
entries.notes: Send data to i2c {device} ; this is comma seperated data, numbers or strings. If a semicolon is used as a seperator e.g. 4137; then the constant is sent as a 16 bit value.

entries.name: isval(
entries.notes: Converts string to number, returns -1 if okay, 0 if fails.

entries.name: iwrite
entries.notes: Write byte to I2C Device Register

entries.name: joycount(
entries.notes: Read the number of attached joypads, not including keyboard emulation of one.

entries.name: joypad(
entries.notes: Reads the current joypad. The return value has bit 0 set if A is pressed, bit 1 set if B is pressed. Values -1,0 or 1 are placed into dx,dy representing movement on the D-Pad. If there is no gamepad plugged in (at the time of writing it doesn't work) the key equivalents are WASDOP and the cursor keys. If [index] is provided it is a specific joypad (from 1,0 is the keyboard), otherwise it is a composite of all of them.

entries.name: key(
entries.notes: Return the state of the given key. The key is the USB HID key scan code.

entries.name: left
entries.notes: Rotate turtle at current position

entries.name: left$(
entries.notes: Left most n characters of a$

entries.name: len(
entries.notes: Return length of string in characters.

entries.name: let
entries.notes: Assignment statement. The LET is optional.

entries.name: library
entries.notes: Librarise / Unlibrarise code.

entries.name: line
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws a line. E.g. LINE 0,0 TO 100,10 TO 120,120 TO 0,0 draws an outline triangle.

entries.name: list
entries.notes: List program to display by line number or procedure name.

entries.name: load
entries.notes: Load file to BASIC space or given address.

entries.name: local
entries.notes: Local variables, use after PROC, restored at ENDPROC variables can

entries.name: locale
entries.notes: Sets the locale to the 2 character country code a$ e.g. locale "de"

entries.name: log(
entries.notes: Natural Logarithm (e.g. ln2) of n.

entries.name: lower$(
entries.notes: Convert a string to lower case

entries.name: max(
entries.notes: Return the largest of a and b (numbers or strings)

entries.name: mid$(
entries.notes: Characters from a$ starting at f (1 indexed), s characters, s is optional and defaults to the rest of the line.

entries.name: min(
entries.notes: Return the smaller of a and b (numbers or strings)

entries.name: mon
entries.notes: Enter the machine code monitor

entries.name: mos
entries.notes: Execute MOS command.

entries.name: mos(
entries.notes: Like the mos command, but returns an non zero error code if the command caused an error.

entries.name: mouse
entries.notes: Select mouse cursor {n} [0 is the default hand pointer]

entries.name: mouse
entries.notes: hide

entries.name: mouse
entries.notes: Position mouse cursor

entries.name: mouse(
entries.notes: Reads the mouse. The return value indicates button state (bit 0 left, bit 1 right), and the mouse position and also the scrolling wheel position are updated into the given variables.

entries.name: move
entries.syntax: move [from x,y] x,y | to x,y | by x,y
entries.notes: Graphics command: sets the current position. Modifiers: from, to, by, ink, solid, frame, dim (see Basic Commands (Graphics)).

entries.name: new
entries.notes: Erase Program

entries.name: next
entries.notes: Ends for loop. The variable parameter is optional. You cannot unwind nested FOR/NEXTs , next must operate in order.

entries.name: noise
entries.notes: To use the white noise feature use the keyword "noise" instead of sound.

entries.name: not
entries.notes: Returns the logical not of a term.

entries.name: notes(
entries.notes: Return the number of notes outstanding on channel c including the one currently playing — so will be zero when the channel goes silent.

entries.name: old
entries.notes: Undoes a new. This can fail depending on what has been done since the 'new'.

entries.name: on
entries.notes: Install an error handler that is called when an error occurs. Effectively this is doing a GOTO that code, so recovery is dependent on what you actually

entries.name: open
entries.notes: output [channel],[file]     | Open a file for input or output on the given channel, using the given file name. Output erases the current file. This gives an error if the file does not exist ; rather than trap this error it is recommended to use the exists() function if you think the file may not be present.

entries.name: page
entries.notes: Return the address of the program base (e.g. the variable table)

entries.name: palette
entries.notes: Set colour c to r,g,b values — these are all 0-255 however it is actually 3:2:3 colour, so they will be approximations.

entries.name: palette
entries.notes: Reset palette to default

entries.name: peek(
entries.notes: Read byte value at a

entries.name: pendown
entries.notes: Draw as the turtle moves in the current colour

entries.name: pendown
entries.notes: Draw as the turtle moves in colour {n}

entries.name: penup
entries.notes: Does not draw as the turtle moves

entries.name: pin
entries.notes: Set UEXT {pin} to given value.

entries.name: pin
entries.notes: output

entries.name: pin(
entries.notes: Return value on UEXT pin n if input, output latch value if output.

entries.name: plot
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws a pixel. Modifiers: from, to, by, ink, solid, frame, dim.

entries.name: point(
entries.notes: Read the screen pixel at coordinates x,y. This is graphics data only.

entries.name: poke
entries.notes: Write byte to address

entries.name: pow(
entries.notes: Returns a raised to the power b ; the result is always floating point.

entries.name: print
entries.notes: Print strings and numbers, standard format - , is used for

entries.name: print
entries.notes: Writes a sequence of expressions to the open file.

entries.name: print
entries.notes: Prints a line to an output channel as an ASCII file, in LF format (e.g. lines are seperated by character code 10). This can be mixed with the above format *but* the sequence has to be the same ; you ann't write a string using print line and read it back with input and vice versa. All variables must be strings.

entries.name: proc
entries.notes: Delimits procedures, optional parameters, must match call. Parameters can be defined as reference parameters and will return values. Parameters cannot be arrays.

entries.name: rand(
entries.notes: Random integer 0 { x { n (e.g. 0 to n-1)

entries.name: read
entries.notes: Read variables from data statements. Types must match those in data statements.

entries.name: rect
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws a rectangle (solid = filled, frame = outline).

entries.name: renumber
entries.notes: Renumber the program from start, or from 1000 by default. This does *not* handle GOTO and GOSUB. Use those, you are on your own.

entries.name: repeat
entries.notes: Execute code until {expr} is true

entries.name: restore
entries.notes: Restore data pointer to program start

entries.name: restore
entries.notes: Restore data pointer to line number

entries.name: return
entries.notes: Return from subroutine called with gosub.

entries.name: right$(
entries.notes: Rightmost n characters of a$

entries.name: rnd(
entries.notes: Random number 0 { x { 1, ignores n.

entries.name: run
entries.notes: Run Program

entries.name: run
entries.notes: Load & Run program.

entries.name: save
entries.notes: Save BASIC program or memory from {adr} length {sz}

entries.name: sfx
entries.notes: Sfx plays sound effects. Sound effects are played immediately as they are usually in response to an event.

entries.name: sin(
entries.notes: Sine of n, n Is in degrees.

entries.name: solid
entries.notes: Fill in rectangles and ellipses. For images and text, forces black background.

entries.name: sound
entries.notes: The Neo6502 has four sound channels, 0-3 which can generate a square wave or white noise sounds. Sound clear: resets the entire sound system, silences all channels, empties all queues. Sound {channel} clear: resets a single channel. Sound {channel},{frequency},{time}[,{slide}]: queues a note on the given channel of the given frequency (in Hz) and time (in centiseconds); the slide value adds that much to the frequency every centisecond.

entries.name: spc(
entries.notes: Returns a string of n spaces.

entries.name: spoint(
entries.notes: Reads the colour index on the sprite layer. 0 is transparency

entries.name: sprite
entries.notes: Sprite commands closely resemble the graphics commands. They begin with SPRITE {n} which sets the working sprite. Options include IMAGE {n} which sets the image, TO {x},{y} which sets the position, FLIP {n} which sets the flip to a number (bit 0 is horizontal flip, bit 1 is vertical flip), ANCHOR {n} which sets the anchor point and BY {x},{y} which sets the position by offset. SPRITE can also take the single command CLEAR ; this resets all sprites and removes them from the display. Up to 128 sprites are supported (sprite 127 is used for the turtle sprite).

entries.name: spritex(
entries.notes: Returns the x coordinate of the sprite's draw position (currently the centre).

entries.name: spritey(
entries.notes: Returns the y coordinate of the sprite's draw position (currently the centre).

entries.name: sqr(
entries.notes: Square root of n

entries.name: sreceive
entries.notes: Send or receive bytes starting at a, count s to SPI device

entries.name: ssend
entries.notes: Send data to SPI device ; this is comma seperated data, numbers or strings. If a semicolon is used as a seperator e.g. 4137; then the constant is sent as a 16 bit value.

entries.name: stop
entries.notes: Halt program with error

entries.name: str$(
entries.notes: Convert n to a string

entries.name: sys
entries.notes: Call 65C02 machine code at given address. Passes contents of variables A,X,Y in those registers.

entries.name: tab(
entries.notes: Advance to screen column n if not past it already.

entries.name: tan(
entries.notes: Tangent of n, n Is in degrees.

entries.name: text
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws text. dim sets the scaling, e.g. text "Hello" dim 2 to 10,10.

entries.name: tiledraw
entries.notes: Graphics command: draws a tilemap (defined by tilemap addr,x,y). Tiles can only be dim 1 or 2 (when 2, tiles are drawn double size giving a 32x32 tile map).

entries.name: tilemap
entries.notes: Define a tilemap. The tilemap data format is in the API. The tilemap is stored in memory at addr, and the offset into the

entries.name: time(
entries.notes: Return time since power on in 100^th^ of a seconds.

entries.name: to
entries.notes: Draw the element at x,y or between the current position and x,y depending on the command. So you could have text "Hello" to 10,10 or rect 0,0 to 100,50

entries.name: true
entries.notes: Return constant -1, improves boolean readability

entries.name: turtle
entries.notes: Reset turtle to home position, facing up the screen.

entries.name: turtle
entries.notes: Hide the turtle

entries.name: turtle
entries.notes: Show the turtle

entries.name: turtle
entries.notes: The turtle is deliberately slowed to give it an animated feel so you can see the drawing, this is because it's primary purpose is educational. This makes it go full speed.

entries.name: uconfig
entries.notes: Set the baud rate and protocol for the UART. Currently only 8N1 is supported.

entries.name: uhasdata(
entries.notes: Return true if there is data in the UART Receive buffer.

entries.name: upper$(
entries.notes: Convert a string to upper case

entries.name: ureceive
entries.notes: Send or receive bytes to/from the UART starting at a, count s

entries.name: usend
entries.notes: Send data to UART ; this is comma seperated data, numbers or strings. If a semicolon is used

entries.name: val(
entries.notes: Convert string to number. Error if bad number.

entries.name: vblanks(
entries.notes: Return the number of vblanks since power on. This is updated at the start of the vblank period.

entries.name: vmode
entries.notes: Sélectionne le mode d'affichage et réinitialise écran, palette et console : 0 = 320×240, 256 couleurs (console 40×30 ; sprites, tilemaps, images) ; 1 = Hercules/MDA 720×350 monochrome, attributs MDA, 2 pages (console 80×25). Hardware error (22) si le firmware ne connaît pas le mode.

entries.name: vmode(
entries.notes: Renvoie le mode d'affichage courant (0 ou 1).

entries.name: wait
entries.notes: Waits for {cs} hundredths of a second

entries.name: while
entries.notes: Repeat code while expression is true

entries.name: who
entries.notes: Display contributors list.
